text: Can my bot read message content without the intent if the user replies to it?
answer:
**Ruling:** Yes, but only for replies to a normal message your bot sent (not a slash command response), and only if the user has "ping on reply" enabled.

**Why:** Discord's three official lists of Message Content intent exceptions disagree, effective from 2026-06-10 (the newest, most specific one):

> "The Message Content intent is **not** needed for your app to access message content in these situations: ... **Replies to your app's messages.** Note: this applies to replies sent using Discord's reply feature to a regular bot message (not an interaction response) and the user has "ping on reply" enabled. It does not apply to replies to slash command responses."

Source: [You Might Not Need a Privileged Intent (developerDocs)](https://docs.discord.com/developers/gateway/you-might-not-need-a-privileged-intent)

The older Gateway docs page (also currently in force, effective from 2022-09-01) lists only four exceptions and does not mention replies at all:

> "Apps **without** the intent will receive empty values in fields that contain user-inputted content with a few exceptions: * Content in messages that an app sends * Content in DMs with the app * Content in which the app is mentioned * Content of the message a message context menu command is used on"

Source: [Gateway (developerDocs)](https://docs.discord.com/developers/events/gateway)

**Watch out:** The dataset's own resolution treats these as complementary, not contradictory: "each page is incomplete rather than wrong." So the reply exception is real but narrow: regular message replies only, ping-on-reply must be on, and it never applies to replies to a slash command's response. For that last case (interaction responses), your bot still needs the Message Content intent to see the reply text.

**Counsel notes:** Test with ping-on-reply toggled off before you ship, since a user with it disabled will silently hand you an empty content field.

text: Can I store user IDs and message content in my database?
answer:
**Ruling:** Yes, but only what your app actually needs for its stated functionality, and only for as long as that functionality needs it.

**Why:** The current Developer Policy, effective from 2024-07-08, ties storage to purpose, not to a blanket permission or ban:

> You may not request, access, or use API Data for any purpose other than as necessary to provide your Application's stated (and approved through App Review, as applicable) functionality; provided that you may also use API Data for the purpose of improving your Application only if it has been aggregated or de-identified such that it cannot be associated with, or used to identify, any individual.

Source: [Discord Developer Policy (current, effective July 8, 2024) (developerPolicy)](https://support-dev.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/8563934450327-Discord-Developer-Policy)

That comes with three companion duties from the current Developer Terms, effective from 2024-07-08:

Delete it once it's no longer needed:
> promptly delete the API Data when: (a) retaining it is no longer necessary for your Application's stated (and approved through App Review, as applicable) functionality that is permitted under the Terms

Encrypt it at rest:
> encryption of the data at rest and (ii) maintaining administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that are designed to prevent unauthorized access and use

Disclose it in a privacy policy:
> You will provide and adhere to a privacy policy for your Application that ... clearly, accurately, and fully describes to users of your Application what data you collect, how you use and share such data with us and third parties, and how users can request deletion of such data.

Source: [Discord Developer Terms of Service (current, effective July 8, 2024) (developerTerms)](https://support-dev.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/8562894815383-Discord-Developer-Terms-of-Service)

**Watch out:** Since you hold MESSAGE_CONTENT, one hard line applies specifically to you, effective from 2024-07-08:

> Do not use message content obtained through the APIs to train machine learning or AI models (including large language models) unless express permission is granted by Discord.

Source: [Discord Developer Policy (current, effective July 8, 2024) (developerPolicy)](https://support-dev.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/8563934450327-Discord-Developer-Policy)

Also, if you're big enough to be in privileged intent review (10,000+ unique users as of the 2026-06-10 threshold change), the review form itself expects you to justify storage:

> If you're storing the data, explain why it's necessary and describe your retention policy and security measures. If you're processing it in memory and discarding it, say so.

Source: [Getting Started with Privileged Intent Review (developer docs)](https://docs.discord.com/developers/gateway/getting-started-with-privileged-intent-review)

There is no fixed retention window in days or months in any current document, so "how long" is judged by necessity, not a countdown.

**Counsel notes:** Store only what your feature needs, write it down in a privacy policy, encrypt it, delete it when the feature no longer needs it, and never let that message content anywhere near a training pipeline.

text: Can I DM users a welcome message when they join?
answer:
**Ruling:** No, not by default. A bot may not DM a user a "welcome" message on join unless that user has personally opted in to receive it.

**Why:** Under the current Developer Policy, effective from 2024-07-08:

> **5. Do not contact users on Discord without their explicit permission.** This includes frequently sending unsolicited direct messages and/or sending direct messages not directly related to maintaining or improving an Application's functionality.

Source: [Discord Developer Policy (current, effective July 8, 2024) (developerPolicy)](https://support-dev.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/8563934450327-Discord-Developer-Policy)

The 2022 edition already flagged this under "Handle data with care":

> No using API Data in ways that go against user expectations, including frequently sending unsolicited DMs

That earlier language is folded into the 2024 wording above, so there is no conflict between editions, just a tightening.

**Watch out:** "Explicit permission" means the individual user opted in, not the server owner enabling a "send welcome DM" toggle in your bot's settings. A member joining a server has not personally consented to be DM'd by your app. If your welcome flow is triggered by the user's own action (for example they ran a slash command or clicked a button to opt in to DMs), that counts as permission and is fine. A blanket on-join DM to everyone does not.

**Counsel notes:** Put the welcome message in a channel instead, or gate the DM behind an explicit opt-in button. Cheaper than explaining "unsolicited" to a policy reviewer.
